item.description:
• Clicking the menu bar icon no longer drags the MacBreeze window in front of whatever you were working in.
  • Each fan's real speed now stays on screen while an app automation is running, instead of disappearing exactly when you want to check it.
  • Changing a rule between "While Running" and "While Frontmost" now takes effect immediately, rather than waiting for that app to quit.
  • New switch on the App Automations page: whether the app you are working in takes the fans from a rule higher in the list, or the list order decides everything.
  • An open fan curve stays open — when you visit another page, and when you quit and come back.
  • The dashboard window now keeps one size, and Preferences can open it centred on screen or put it away when you switch desktop.
  • This window now lists every version you missed, not only the newest one, and opens in the middle of the screen.
  • The dashboard dims behind this window, and the current-temperature dot on the fan curve is no longer hidden by its own dashed line.

• When an app automation is in charge of the fans, the menu bar panel says so once, right under the title, with that app's icon. Click it to open the automation.
  • The profile picker and status line step aside while an automation runs, instead of showing the app's name as if it were a profile.
  • The menu bar panel's header now carries MacBreeze's own menu bar icon.
  • After each update, MacBreeze shows what changed, in a window like this one.

Fixed

  • Fan controls looked frozen in the menu bar. While an app automation is running, MacBreeze locks the fan settings so the rule stays in charge — but the menu bar never said so. It now tells you which app is in control, and gives you a link straight to App Automations to change it.
  • The trial-ended notice could be missed. MacBreeze only checked your licence when it started, so if your trial ended while it was running you weren't told until you next restarted it. It now checks once a day.

Privacy

MacBreeze now records the day your Mac last checked its licence, and whether it's on a trial, the free version, or a paid licence, so we can count how many people use it. Nothing about how you use the app is recorded, and the record deletes itself after 90 days without a check-in. The details are in the privacy policy at macbreeze.app.
